body:
APPROVED BY MYK IN CHAT, 2026-07-26, as the exploration half of the erasure-seam pair (T100). BACKGROUND PRIORITY: this churns when nothing hotter is unblocked, and it is exploration — the deliverable is a design, not code.

FIRST LINE, SAME AS T100'S: **the promise is untouched.** Full provable erasure stays (Myk, 2026-07-25, closed). Crypto-shredding here is DEFENSE IN DEPTH UNDERNEATH that promise — the byte sweep remains load-bearing and verified; the keys make what the sweep chases worthless faster. Any draft that reads as replacing the sweep with key deletion has failed before review.

THE IDEA: store drivers hold deltas encrypted at rest, keyed per delta (or per subject/batch — a design question below). Purge destroys the key FIRST, then sweeps bytes as today. The seam shrinks because every place bytes linger beyond the primary row — WAL residue that waits for a checkpoint, archive fans, mirror copies, quarantine-pool copies, crash-left temp files — becomes ciphertext noise the instant the key dies. holds() gains a cheap local half (key gone = unreadable everywhere at once) while keeping its byte half; T67's truncation debt and T66's displaced-bytes-in-the-WAL note both stop being sharp.

HARD CONSTRAINTS: rhizomatic is frozen — this lives entirely inside StoreBackend drivers; content addresses remain addresses of PLAINTEXT delta bytes (the ciphertext is a driver detail, exactly like sqlite's page format); federation is unaffected (the wire carries plaintext deltas as today, each store encrypting its own rest). The genesis/boot path must still work with the keystore sealed or absent — decide what a store WITHOUT its keystore is (bricked? read-refusing? H9 says: it reports unprovable, never clean).

THE COST TO DESIGN HONESTLY, because it is the whole decision: **the keystore becomes the erasure trust root.** Key management is now where the promise lives — keystore backup vs erasure (a backed-up key un-shreds; an unbacked keystore loss is total), key derivation (per-delta keys are cheap if derived from a master + delta id, but then destroying ONE derived key requires the derivation to be non-recomputable — a real cryptographic design point, probably a per-delta random key wrapped by a master, with the WRAP destroyed on purge), the keystore's own at-rest story, and what holds() means for a tier that has bytes but no key. Performance: a decrypt per delta read lands on the H8-sensitive full-scan paths — measure, and say what it costs on a 100k-delta store.

PRIOR ART TO CONSULT, briefly, in the design doc: standard crypto-shredding literature (GDPR-driven), sqlite encryption extensions vs app-layer encryption of the delta blob column (prefer the latter — driver-owned, no new native deps), and what the browser driver does (LocalStorage + WebCrypto, and whether the tutorial's open-a-store-in-a-tab story survives a keystore).

DELIVERABLE: a design document — likely a subsection of §32 (T100) or its own working spec — with the key-lifecycle state machine, the holds() semantics table, the failure modes (keystore lost, key backed up when it should not be, purge crash between key-destroy and sweep), and a measured decrypt-cost estimate. Then STOP for Myk: this changes what the system's erasure DEPENDS ON, which is his call even though the promise itself is unchanged. Relations: T100 is the frame; T67/T66's journal and hazard entries are the residue catalogue this exists to shrink.
title: Crypto-shredding at rest — shrink the erasure seam without touching the promise (BACKGROUND)
